\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{شكوى} (shakwā)}{شكوى (shakwā)}]{\ar{شكوى} (shakwā) — a complaint}

\label{lesson:AR-C449-shakwa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to calm down, then the Arabic for to complain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{شكوى}}
\textbf{\ar{شكوى}} — \emph{shakwā} — \textquotedblleft{}a complaint\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كتب} \ar{أبي} \ar{شكوى} \ar{إلى} \ar{المدير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kataba abī shakwā ilā al-mudīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father wrote a complaint to the manager.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{شكوى}} (\emph{shakwā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-k-w}, \textquotedblleft{}to complain\textquotedblright{} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shakwā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shakwā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kataba abī shakwā ilā al-mudīr.} — My father wrote a complaint to the manager.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to calm down, then the Arabic for to complain, then say \emph{shakwā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{شكوى} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A complaint\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تعويض} (taʿwīḍ)}{تعويض (taʿwīḍ)}]{\ar{تعويض} (taʿwīḍ) — compensation}

\label{lesson:AR-C449-tawid}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to complain, then the Arabic for a complaint.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تعويض}}
\textbf{\ar{تعويض}} — \emph{taʿwīḍ} — \textquotedblleft{}compensation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{طلب} \ar{المسافرون} \ar{تعويضا} \ar{بعد} \ar{التأخير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṭalaba al-musāfirūn taʿwīḍan baʿda at-taʾkhīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The travellers asked for compensation after the delay.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تعويض}} (\emph{taʿwīḍ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-w-ḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}to give in exchange\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the verbal noun of Form II; an \emph{ʿiwaḍ} is a thing given in place of another.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʿwīḍ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʿwīḍ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭalaba al-musāfirūn taʿwīḍan baʿda at-taʾkhīr.} — The travellers asked for compensation after the delay.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to complain, then the Arabic for a complaint, then say \emph{taʿwīḍ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تعويض} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Compensation\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عوض} (ʿawwaḍa)}{عوض (ʿawwaḍa)}]{\ar{عوض} (ʿawwaḍa) — to compensate}

\label{lesson:AR-C449-awwada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a complaint, then the Arabic for compensation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عوض}}
\textbf{\ar{عوض}} — \emph{ʿawwaḍa} — \textquotedblleft{}to compensate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{عوضت} \ar{الشركة} \ar{الركاب} \ar{عن} \ar{التأخير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ʿawwaḍat ash-sharika ar-rukkāb ʿan at-taʾkhīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The company compensated the passengers for the delay.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يعوض}, \emph{yuʿawwiḍ}.

Someone is compensated \emph{ʿan} a loss.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عوض}} (\emph{ʿawwaḍa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-w-ḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}to give in exchange\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿawwaḍa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿawwaḍat ash-sharika ar-rukkāb ʿan at-taʾkhīr.} — The company compensated the passengers for the delay.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a complaint, then the Arabic for compensation, then say \emph{ʿawwaḍa} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تذمر} (tadhammara)}{تذمر (tadhammara)}]{\ar{تذمر} (tadhammara) — to grumble}

\label{lesson:AR-C449-tadhammara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for compensation, then the Arabic for to compensate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تذمر}}
\textbf{\ar{تذمر}} — \emph{tadhammara} — \textquotedblleft{}to grumble\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تذمر} \ar{أخي} \ar{من} \ar{الطعام} \ar{في} \ar{الفندق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tadhammara akhī min aṭ-ṭaʿām fī al-funduq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother grumbled about the food in the hotel.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتذمر}, \emph{yatadhammar}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تذمر}} (\emph{tadhammara}) is usually traced to the native Arabic root \emph{dh-m-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to be angry, to growl\textquotedblright{}. It is Form V.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tadhammara}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for compensation, then the Arabic for to compensate, then say \emph{tadhammara} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استبدل} (istabdala)}{استبدل (istabdala)}]{\ar{استبدل} (istabdala) — to swap; to exchange (for another)}

\label{lesson:AR-C449-istabdala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to compensate, then the Arabic for to grumble.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استبدل}}
\textbf{\ar{استبدل}} — \emph{istabdala} — \textquotedblleft{}to swap; to exchange (for another)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{استبدلت} \ar{القميص} \ar{بقميص} \ar{أكبر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{istabdaltu al-qamīṣ bi-qamīṣ akbar.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I swapped the shirt for a bigger one.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يستبدل}, \emph{yastabdil}.

In modern use the new thing takes \emph{bi-}; classical usage put \emph{bi-} on the thing given up.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استبدل}} (\emph{istabdala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{b-d-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to change, to replace\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form X.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}
